statement: cursor .now returns the full fold of every op
cursor .atOp(id) derives the prefix THROUGH that op — the target op's own effect is APPLIED, not excluded
reachability: LIVE — RewindWindow scrub positions; since the M4-RW-002 fix (7e5e486610, 2026-08-08) HistoryPane's 'Rewind to before this…' posts the PREDECESSOR op, so the inclusive boundary composes with the label instead of contradicting it

statement: a cursor whose op id is not present in `ops` silently returns the FULL derivation — the requested moment is replaced by the present, with no signal of any kind
reachability: UNTRACED as a writer gesture — RewindWindow reads the same _opLogMirror restoreToOp derives from, so the cursor is normally in the log by construction; I found no compaction path that removes an op from the mirror

statement: an empty op array derives an empty state under either cursor
restoring to op X leaves X's own effect present in the document — the method's contract is 'the state it had immediately AFTER the op was applied', and the code matches its doc comment exactly
the appended op is a .checkpointRestore stamped provenance.synthesisSource = .rewind with sourceCheckpoint = the target op id (the field is overloaded: a past op id, not a checkpoint id)
when the target IS the tip the restore is a genuine no-op: restoreOp is nil, the counts are equal, and the log is not extended
reachability: LIVE — RewindWindow deliberately ENABLES Restore on .atOp(latestOpId); RewindCursor.swift documents that as intentional

statement: a target op id that is NOT IN THE LOG produces a RewindRestoreResult that compares EQUAL to the legitimate no-op above, and nothing is thrown: no channel carries the difference between 'there was nothing to do' and 'the moment you asked for does not exist'
reachability: UNTRACED as a writer gesture — same trace as M4-RW-003

statement: the result reports priorSequenceCount, newSequenceCount and the removed paragraph ids
the op log is append-only across a rewind: every pre-rewind op survives and the log strictly grows; nothing is truncated or compacted
every word the rewind took away stays derivable at the pre-rewind tip: Deriver.derive(ops:upTo: preTip) reproduces the pre-rewind paragraphs exactly
rewinding FORWARD again returns the live document to the exact pre-rewind words
the orphan sweep archives every OPEN annotation anchored to a paragraph the rewind removed, and reports their op ids in archivedAnnotationOpIds
reachability: LIVE — any rewind past the creation of an annotated paragraph

statement: an annotation on a paragraph that SURVIVES the rewind is untouched

the `ann.kind != .craftNote` carve-out cannot change any outcome: a craft note has NO paragraph anchor, so the `removed.contains` term is already false. Three independent sites force it doc-scoped — add_craft_note's MCP schema has no paragraph_id property and passes nil, Document.addAnnotation writes `changes: []` for .craftNote, and AnnotationDeriver forces paragraphId = nil for that kind regardless
reachability: NOT REACHABLE — there is no surface that can give a craft note a paragraph anchor

statement: a document that has never had an annotation op gets no sweep flagged, and no stale removed-set leaks into an annotation created after a later rewind

an accepted suggestion whose changes-carrying accept lies PAST the target, on a paragraph that SURVIVES, is returned to .open by a changes-free .claudeAcceptRevert and reported in reopenedAnnotationOpIds — so the annotation's status and the manuscript text agree again
reachability: LIVE — accept a suggestion, then rewind past the accept

statement: the same accept on a paragraph the rewind REMOVED is archived instead (a .claudeArchive), reported in archivedAnnotationOpIds — an open suggestion on a nonexistent paragraph would not be actionable

rewinding FORWARD past the moment a paragraph was created brings the paragraph, the pane task AND the sweep-archived annotation back: the restore appends a `.rewind`-stamped `.annotationReopen` for every annotation whose latest lifecycle op is a rewind-stamped archive from an open status and whose anchor paragraph exists in the target state (RULING-25)
reachability: LIVE — two consecutive Restores from the rewind modal, the second targeting a later op
fix_history: Pinned the ASYMMETRY (comment stayed archived, permanently and silently) until fixed at 12d763c95a, 2026-08-08, under RULING-25

statement: rewoundTaskOps is true when task-lifecycle ops lie after the target and false on a forward rewind

um.removeAllActions() runs UNCONDITIONALLY before the restore, so a rewind that turns out to be a genuine no-op destroys the writer's whole typing-undo stack and registers nothing in its place — canUndo is false and the action name is empty afterwards
reachability: LIVE — the modal's Restore button is enabled on .atOp(latestOpId) by design, which is exactly this case, one click away

statement: a target that does not exist in the log destroys the typing-undo stack, changes nothing, and returns a success value
reachability: UNTRACED as a writer gesture — same trace as M4-RW-003

statement: a rewind that changes something leaves exactly ONE undo action, named 'Restore from History'
one ⌘Z of that action returns the whole rewind — text, reopened accepts and sweep-archived annotations together
the compensating restore is stamped .undoRewind, never .rewind, so it is invisible to TaskDeriver's rewind-window matcher and no second .rewind stamp appears

when the text has drifted since the restore the undo DECLINES: it leaves the drifted text alone, does not restore forward, throws nothing to the caller, and writes only to documentLog — the writer presses ⌘Z on a menu item reading 'Undo Restore from History' and nothing happens
reachability: LIVE — a cross-device merge landing between the restore and the ⌘Z; directly exercised by the shipped RewindUndoTests.test_restore_undo_afterForeignOps_isLoudNoOp, where 'loud' means loud to the log

statement: the result carries every collateral effect the rewind caused — the removed paragraphs, the annotations archived, the ones reopened, whether tasks were rewound, and the sequence counts either side

a rewind whose manuscript text is unchanged but whose range contains task-lifecycle ops still appends a marker .checkpointRestore with empty changes, so TaskDeriver can slice at the boundary and the pane task disappears
redo re-runs restoreToOp from scratch rather than replaying, so a redo can never disagree with a fresh rewind

scope: HistoryPane.predecessorIndex + the 'Rewind to before this…' deep-link
statement: 'Rewind to before this…' resolves to the row op's immediate predecessor in the opId-ordered log, so the opened cursor derives state EXCLUDING the selected op's effect; the first op (no predecessor) offers no deep-link

source.ref: MaughamTests/Views/HistoryPaneRewindTargetTests.test_rewindBeforeThis_excludesTheTargetOpsOwnEffect — a PERMANENT production test, not an experiment copy: the fix's own regression net

reachability: LIVE — every History row with a manuscript-mutating op and a predecessor
out_of_module_note: Lives in Maugham/Views, not the three rewind files — added here because it is the composition claim that makes M4-RW-002's flipped filing honest

scope: Document.restoreToOp — the return journey's scope guard
statement: an annotation the WRITER archived (no synthesisSource on the archive op) stays archived across a full backward-and-forward travel; only Maugham's own rewind-stamped archives reopen

undoing a forward travel re-archives what the travel reopened — via the compensating restore's own step-7 sweep, no bespoke undo work; redo re-runs the forward restore and reopens again. The return journey is gated to `.rewind` restores so the `.undoRewind` compensating restore never double-acts
